findings.title: Save Settings now posts without the General fields, so every save silently resets General settings to defaults
findings.problem: The diff removes id="settings-form" from the instances form (line 134) and removes form="settings-form" from every General field. It also moves those fields into their own <form> (lines 18-90). The only 'Save Settings' button (line 241) is inside the instances form, so its POST no longer includes log_level, hard_max_per_cycle, max_history_rows, request_timeout, page_size, tracking_window_minutes, max_consecutive_failures or skip_unreleased. save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:529-540) does not fall back to current_settings for these. It builds them with safe_int(form.get(...), <hardcoded default>) and safe_log_level(form.get('log_level')). Then skip_unreleased = form.get('skip_unreleased') == 'on' becomes False. Pydantic accepts all of these values, so they are written to the TOML at routes.py:608-610. Result: any save of instance settings resets General to defaults, and the user sees no error. This reverts the fix in HEAD commit 542d5dd.
findings.fix_hint: restore id="settings-form" on the instances form and form="settings-form" on each General input/select, keeping the General section in a non-form <div>
findings.why_it_matters: Saving an API key or URL change quietly wipes the user's General config (for example skip_unreleased turns off and the item caps change), which changes how searches run with no visible error.

findings.title: This diff undoes fix 542d5dd: clicking 'Save Settings' resets every General setting to its default
findings.problem: The diff puts the General fields back inside their own <form action=save_settings> (line 18 to line 90), and that form has no submit button. It also removes id="settings-form" from the instances form (line 134) and drops the form="settings-form" attribute from all 8 General controls. The only 'Save Settings' button (lines 241-243) is inside the instances form, so clicking it sends only the instance fields. save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:529-541) builds the whole general block from the request with defaults for missing keys. Each instance save therefore writes log_level='info', hard_max_per_cycle=0, max_history_rows=1000, request_timeout=30, page_size=50, tracking_window_minutes=60, max_consecutive_failures=5 and skip_unreleased=False to config.toml, and the scheduler reloads with those values. This is exactly the bug described in commit 542d5dd, so the diff is a straight revert of that fix.

findings.fix_hint: Throw away this working-tree change (git checkout triggarr/templates/settings.html). That brings back form="settings-form" on the General controls and id="settings-form" on the instances form.
findings.why_it_matters: Saving any instance quietly overwrites the operator's General config. skip_unreleased flips to False, which starts searches for unreleased items. max_history_rows goes back to 1000, so history gets pruned. Every user of the settings page is affected, and nothing on screen says it happened.

members.title: Reverts General-section form to the exact broken pattern CLAUDE.md's own convention and a prior fix commit rejected
members.problem: Root CLAUDE.md: 'before introducing a new pattern, check how the same problem is solved elsewhere in the repo and follow that.' This diff removes the documented, tested pattern (General fields carry form="settings-form" to associate with the Save button in the separate instances <form id="settings-form">) and replaces it with a standalone <form> wrapping only the General section, with no submit button inside it. A browser only submits a form's own associated controls, so clicking 'Save Settings' drops every General field, exactly the bug description in commit 542d5dd.
members.why_it_matters: This is a verified regression: commit 542d5dd fixed this exact bug and added a regression test in tests/test_web.py that will fail, and in production every General setting silently resets on every save.
members.fix_hint: Restore the prior committed pattern: give the instances form back id="settings-form", remove the new standalone General <form> wrapper (back to a plain <div>), and put form="settings-form" back on every General input/select/checkbox so they submit with the Save Settings button.

members.title: This change undoes fix 542d5dd: General fields are back in a form with no Save button, so saving never sends them
members.problem: The working-tree diff puts back exactly the structure HEAD's commit 542d5dd removed. The General fields go back into their own <form action=save_settings> (lines 18-90), and that form has no submit control. The only 'Save Settings' button (line 241) sits in the second save_settings form (line 134), and this diff also drops that form's id="settings-form". The file already solves 'can't nest forms' another way: each control carries a form= attribute pointing at a form outside the main one (the add-instance controls at lines 230-232 point at <form id="add-{{app_name}}"> at line 250, and the General fields used form="settings-form" until this diff). The diff drops that pattern for the General fields.

members.fix_hint: Discard this working-tree change (git checkout triggarr/templates/settings.html). That restores id="settings-form" on the instances form and form="settings-form" on every General control.

members.title: Restore General fields to the Save Settings submission
members.problem: The Save Settings button at lines 241-244 now submits only the instance form; General controls belong to a separate form with no submit button. The unchanged handler at triggarr/web/routes.py:531-539 replaces missing General values with defaults and persists them. For example, saving an instance with hard_max_per_cycle=10 and skip_unreleased=true configured now writes 0 (unlimited) and false, removing the configured cap and release filtering. General edits are also omitted. Previously, explicit form associations included these values in the same submission.
members.why_it_matters: Saving an instance now writes default General values over the operator's configured ones and discards General edits.
members.fix_hint: Restore the settings-form ID and General controls' form associations. Verify the existing form-association test and add a submission regression check that nondefault General values survive saving instance settings.

members.title: General settings form has no submit button and cannot be submitted
members.problem: The new General <form> (lines 18-90) has no submit button. It holds several number inputs, so HTML implicit submission is blocked: pressing Enter in a form with no submit button and more than one such field does nothing. The user cannot save changes to log level, caps, timeouts or skip_unreleased from this form at all. Even if submitted, its POST would carry no instance fields, so save_settings would take the preserve-existing-instances branch (routes.py:581-594). Because nothing submits, General edits are lost.
members.why_it_matters: Users cannot change General settings from the UI at all.
members.fix_hint: associate the General fields with the single Save Settings form via form="settings-form" (as before), rather than wrapping them in a separate form with no submit button
